# BACKGROUND 2 · EARTH ZOOM OUT + GLOBE 360° (storyboard scenes 7–9)
**Era (brief):** Sc 7–8 = **base** kawaii style · Sc 9 = the red wave passes → **1950s** first-colour features (Toei: Hakujaden 1958, Magic Boy 1959), with the globe as a **gouache storybook painting**. The era dropdown offers base · 1950s only.
**Deadline (plan):** week 2 · Fri 16 Oct 2026.

## Shots
1. **Sc 7–8 · jump & fall** (base): from the characters' spot on the dome, the camera follows the jump path (an invisible point) over the dome edge and drops toward the sea. A clear lane (no buildings or trees, 10 units wide) runs from the dome to the sea so the camera never passes through anything. → Panorama: a tall vertical strip of the fall (near-orthographic, no smear).
2. **Zoom out** (base): one continuous move street → city → coastline → continent → globe. Log-scale speed: distance = exp(lerp(ln 30, ln 4200, ease(t))); the camera's up vector blends from the local ground normal to world up, so the globe ends upright. → Single 4K frames (no camera travel to stitch).
3. **Sc 9 · red wave → 1950s**: the globe framed, the red wave sweeps and the whole picture becomes 1950s gouache.
4. **Globe 360° turntable** (1950s): a locked camera, one turn per 24 s, clouds on their own shell turning ×1.15 faster, a soft day/night terminator, warm night-light dots on the dark side, a soft atmosphere rim. → **Panorama: one long strip of the turning globe**: centre-column slices of a near-orthographic view (camera 60,000 units away, narrow lens) while the globe turns, i.e. the globe surface unrolled, ready for a 2D pan behind a round mask. The clouds are stitched with the land; slide the cloud layer (its own element PNG) 15% faster when compositing.

## The world (kawaii + 1950s gouache)
- An upright globe (R 1000), equirectangular **CanvasTexture** painted procedurally: recognisable but simplified continents with soft, rounded coastlines (drawn from coarse lon/lat outlines, blurred and thresholded for round edges), flat colour areas (greens, sand deserts, pale ochre, white poles), teal-blue sea, paper / gouache grain.
- **Land and sea are separate meshes** (a land shell just above the sea sphere, alpha-masked), so they export as separate PNGs. **Coastlines get lineart** (the land shell writes an id colour in the normal pass).
- The **city** sits on a temperate east coast (≈ 40° N), in a local frame on the globe surface. It is a small 1950s advanced-city island in the same language as BG 1: the cream dome where the characters jump, low/mid-rise blocks with windows and rooftop water tanks, a few modest towers, round trees, a beach ring, a harbour pier. Small round **islands** nearby (Kirby Everbay Coast map) for the coastline beat.
- **Space**: deep navy-teal, never pitch black; soft round stars (Points); the **Moon** as a cute cream sphere with a few soft crater discs (Doraemon *Moon Exploration* 2019).
- Sky colour blends with altitude: Kirby sky blue near the ground → navy in space.

No build step, no server, no external assets except these CDN scripts: Three.js r170 (importmap from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/`, including `examples/jsm/` addons and `lil-gui`) and JSZip 3.10.1. All CSS, JS, shaders and procedural textures are inline.

The team's quick 3D mockup (Snow) shows two coloured spheres standing in for the characters: ignore them, because they would cover the background that has to be painted. Mark where the characters will stand with an overlay-only staging guide (dashed box, off by default, never exported), and keep that spot calm and low in contrast.
- A fixed, always-visible **EXPORT BAR** (bottom of the screen, big labelled buttons, never hidden in a menu):
  1. **Export 4K Panorama PNG**: the whole shot as ONE LONG PANORAMA (see below), final colour look.
  2. **Panorama Lineart**: lines only, transparent background (option: white background).
  3. **Panorama Base color**: flat fills only (no light, shadow, fog, lines, grain or vignette), clean areas for the magic wand.
  4. **ZIP · each element**: one PNG per element (city, trees, hills, clouds, rocks…) for each pass (colour / lineart / base colour), plus the full image, all in one ZIP, with a README listing the elements.

One group per element; flat pieces with their colour/texture; ink lines as edges; the shot camera "ShotCamera" animated over the shot at 24 fps (position + rotation). Two modes: **instanced** (default, small file of a few MB: each instanced batch is split per colour and exported with `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing`, which Blender 3.6+ imports as linked copies) and **baked** (one mesh per element with vertex colours, for older Blender). Opens with *File › Import › glTF 2.0*.

# LONG PANORAMA EXPORT (required)
- The PNG is one continuous painting of the whole camera move, 2160 px tall (4K height). The width grows with the move (a full 360° turn at 45° vertical FOV ≈ 17,000 px). A vertical move gives a tall strip, 3840 px wide.
- How to build it: render thin slices (≈256 px + 12 px margin each side) from the centre of the frame with `camera.setViewOffset`, advance the camera parameter by exactly the slice width in pixels, and stitch the slices side by side on a 2D canvas. Cap any side at 32,000 px.
- **No breaks, no smear** (these come from parallax when a moving camera is stitched):
  - **Turns / pans**: stitch a camera that **turns in place** (same position, height, pitch and lens as the shot). A pure rotation gives a perfectly seamless cylindrical strip. For an orbit shot, turn in place at the orbit centre; the orbit's depth comes back from the per-element layers (multiplane).
  - **Tracks / descents / side scrolls / a turning globe**: stitch a **near-orthographic** version of the view (the same framing from very far away with a narrow lens, e.g. 3,000–60,000 units, with fog distances shifted by the same amount so the colours do not change). Every slice is then a true flat strip, layers never smear, and loops match exactly.
- A panorama is ONE painting: no vignette, no transition wipe, no smear, no 4-box split while stitching. The era look is the one active at the current time.
- Each shot declares its own panorama (`from`, `to`, `axis`, `pxPerUnit`, `setup(s)`). A shot without camera travel falls back to a single 4K frame.

# ELEMENTS (one PNG each)
- Every object belongs to a named element (for example: sky, clouds, hills, ground, river, dome, rocks, logs, grass, flowers, trees, houses, city, landmark, poles, cars, street…). The GUI lists them with visibility checkboxes.
- Element PNGs use a **holdout**: the element is drawn normally and everything else only writes depth (invisible). Each PNG therefore contains only what the camera really sees of that element, and stacking all element PNGs of a pass rebuilds the full image exactly, in any order.
- Element lineart = the drawn lines that touch that element (mask the edge lines with the element's coverage, slightly dilated).

# LINEART: EVERYTHING HAS LINES, ALL THE SAME WIDTH
- Every element has lineart, including flat things (roads, river banks, ponds, windows, coastlines) and small details (dashes, grass tufts, wires).
- One line width for the whole image: **2.4 px at 1080p**, scaled with the output height (4.8 px at 2160). Nothing may come out too thick or too thin, near or far.
  - Edge lines: a screen-space Sobel pass on a normal + depth render (half-width = line width / 2 in real pixels).
  - Flat decals and windows: in that normal pass they output a unique flat "id colour", so their borders become lines too.
  - Hand-drawn marks (dashes, tufts, wires): `LineSegments2` + `LineMaterial` with `worldUnits: false` and `linewidth` = the same pixel width, so it is constant at any distance.
  - Inverted-hull silhouettes are optional only ("extra silhouette", off by default), because they would double the outer line.
- Ink colour **#8A6B64** (from the team's own city test), with options for dark brown #5A3A30 or black. Lines are composited AFTER the era grade, so they never get recoloured (grey in B&W eras). In the colour render, lines fade slightly with fog distance. The colour render has no wobble; lineart has an optional small hand wobble.

# NOTHING CUT OFF, NOTHING BARE
- No element may be cut off in a weird way: clouds, towers and landmarks sit fully inside the frame and the camera range (no clouds clipped by a cylinder or texture edge). Keep **open sky above the tallest roofs**: limit heights by distance to the camera so every roof stays ≈10° below the top of the frame.
- Clouds are never generic: mix big cumulus, medium clusters and small puffs (4–8 puffs each, bigger in the middle, flat bottoms like Chiikawa clouds) at varied distances and heights, each one placed so it stays whole inside the frame.
- Any camera move must have a clear lane: the camera never passes through a building or tree.
- Nothing is plain or empty. Even simple surfaces carry small, simple details: hills get rocks, fallen logs, stumps and dead branches, grass clumps, flowers and Chiikawa-style dashes; cities get windows, rooftop props, street furniture, cars; walls and floors get props.

# PROJECT CONTEXT: "Sirpeltric" (SirPeltric Studio)
One continuous camera journey through anime history. Each background carries the scene into the next era:
1945 black & white → 1950s first colour → 1960s TV limited animation → 1970s warm cel → 1980s saturated OVA → 1990s late cel / early digital → full-colour painterly → a final grey warp that fades to black. Every era change passes through a **red wave line** (a wavy red line sweeps across the frame, with the new era applied behind it).

**Keep the years exactly as in the brief.** Each background uses only the eras of its own storyboard scenes (the era dropdown lists only those). Architecture and props must match that era as an **advanced city / place of that time** (not one country's rules). Tall buildings existed but were rare, and nothing should look like a later decade.

- Kawaii & simple, with the feel of Kirby and Chiikawa. Not realistic, not overly detailed.

- Colourful and lively, with an overall happy, cozy tone.

# ERA TREATMENTS (one full-screen ShaderPass, `uEra` A/B + transition)
- **base**: kawaii base style, no filter.
- **1945** B&W wartime feature: luminance quantised to #111111 #3A3A3A #6E6E6E #A8A8A8 #E8E4DA; vignette, grain, flicker.
- **1950s** first colour features (Toei): soft gouache, pastel #2F4A5C #6E9C9A #D9C7A0 #C0704B #F2E6CF, paper texture.
- **1960s** TV limited animation: flat colour, posterised, bold outline, #1F3A68 #3E7CB1 #F2C14E #D94A38 #F4F1E8.
- **1970s** warm cel / poster paint: #4B3B2A #7A8B3C #C98B3A #D9B98A #5B8DB8, warm tint, grain, brush texture.
- **1980s** saturated OVA: #1B1446 #5B2A86 #E94F8A #F29E4C #7ED3E6, airbrushed glow (bloom), neon nights.
- **1990s** late cel / early digital: #1E2A30 #3F6E73 #8FB3A8 #D8C9A3 #B04A3A, teal haze, subtle grain.
- **colour** full-colour painterly (Ghibli / Kazuo Oga): #2E5E3A #6BA368 #F2D17B #4F8FC0 #F6EFE0.
- **warp**: greys, then fade to black.
- Transitions: red wave (linear sweep), red wave rotating 360°, colour bleed (fade), crack (halves split, the next era shows in the gap).
- Base colour export = each object's flat colour mapped through the active era palette on the CPU (same maths as the shader).

# TECH SPEC
- **Flat 2D fills (default)**: every shape is ONE flat colour (unlit, like a cel painting / Chiikawa field / Kirby pixel scene). Depth tint (fog) is taken per object from its origin, so a shape never carries a gradient; big flat ground pieces get fog in a few hard steps. The sky is a few flat bands. The scene light colour/strength becomes one flat tint, so mood presets still work. Options: *flat + one cel shadow* (Kirby) and the old *soft 3D toon* (`MeshToonMaterial`, 3-step gradient 150/208/255).
- Light page: preview pixel ratio ≤ 1.5 with auto step-down when slow, render only when something changes, minified Three.js + modulepreload, JSZip and GLTFExporter loaded only when exporting.
- Rounded geometry only: `SphereGeometry`, `CapsuleGeometry`, `RoundedBoxGeometry`, `LatheGeometry`, extruded rounded gables. No sharp boxes (except hidden helpers).
- Many copies go into `InstancedMesh` batches per (group, geometry, element) with per-instance colours.
- Timeline: shots with play/pause, a scrub slider, a shot list, and a lens readout (mm). The era per shot follows the brief; the GUI can override it for previews.
- Guides (screen only): rule of thirds, title/action safe, horizon / eye line, vanishing point, staging guide.
- 16:9 stage, responsive (laptop and tablet), devicePixelRatio ≤ 2, deterministic seeded random so every export matches the preview.
